input.quote: (b) Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV(b) is the only audit right binding us, with the cost allocation sitting separately in p0064. Two good features are already present: the auditor must be an independent CPA or Audit Professional selected by mutual agreement, and Licensor bears audit cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found (the preferred cost threshold). However, the clause imposes no frequency limit (Licensor may request audits repeatedly) and gives no advance notice period — the "within 30 days of receipt of a written request" language is a deadline for us to submit to the audit, not notice to us. It therefore fails the fallback on frequency and notice, approaching the unlimited-audit walk-away, and is also silent on business hours, auditor confidentiality, off-site conduct and system access. We have made the shortest edit to the preferred level, leaving the independent-auditor and 5% cost terms untouched.

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
mappings.quote: Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records

mappings.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
mappings.quote: The cost of the audit will be borne by Licensor unless a discrepancy of more than five-percent (5%) is discovered, in which case the cost of the audit shall be borne by Licensee.

mappings.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality, off-site and no-system-access limits to the Licensor audit right
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The audit right currently has no frequency or notice limit and no controls on scope, so we have capped audits at once in any 12-month period on 30 days' written notice during business hours, and required off-site conduct where possible, a confidentiality-bound auditor and no direct access to our systems. The existing independent-auditor selection and the 5% cost-shifting threshold are unchanged.

ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
ops.newText: Any such audit shall be permitted no more than once in any 12-month period, during business hours, and upon at least 30 days' written notice from Licensor.

ops.text: Each such audit shall be conducted off-site where possible, by an auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, and Licensor shall have no direct access to Licensee's systems.
